title: Buffer Stocks and FCI

segments.say: Why does the government keep millions of tonnes of grain in store, even in good years?

anim.title: Grain into the central pool
items: Farmers sell at the minimum support price
FCI and state agencies buy and store it
It is issued for schemes, or sold in the open market

segments.say: Farmers sell wheat and rice at the minimum support price. The Food Corporation of India and state agencies buy and store it in what is called the central pool.

anim.title: A buffer has two parts
items: Strategic reserve: 20 lakh t rice + 30 lakh t wheat

segments.say: The government sets a buffer norm in two parts: an operational stock for regular needs, and a strategic reserve of twenty lakh tonnes of rice and thirty of wheat.
The norm changes through the year. It is highest on the first of July, after the spring wheat purchases, at about four hundred and eleven lakh tonnes.
The grain is kept in warehouses and covered stacks run by FCI, the Central Warehousing Corporation and state agencies.
Stocks often run far above it: on the first of July twenty twenty-five, about seven hundred and thirty-seven lakh tonnes. Extra grain can be sold in the open market to cool prices.
For GS Three, a buffer stock does two jobs: food security in a bad year, and a check on prices in any year.

sources: PIB, 7 February 2020 (PRID 1602455): stocking norms for the central pool (operational stock plus strategic reserve of 20 LMT rice and 30 LMT wheat), totals 210.40 LMT on 1 April, 411.20 on 1 July, 307.70 on 1 October, 214.10 on 1 January; storage capacity with FCI, CWC and state agencies including covered and plinth (CAP) storage; under OMSS(D) FCI sells excess stock in the open market at pre-determined prices, decided with reference to MSP, economic cost and surplus stocks
PIB, 22 July 2025 (PRID 2146811): buffer norm on 1 July 2025 of 411.20 lakh tonnes against central pool stocks of 736.61 lakh tonnes; stocks above buffer norms

reviewNote: Facts are from two PIB releases. 'After the spring wheat purchases' explains the July peak; it is an inference, not a quote. 'Issued for schemes' in the flow is general; NFSA and PMGKAY are not named because no source for them was read. The FCI depot photo may show the FCI logo on its board; crop it out. Moving facts: stock levels change monthly; the norms date from 2017.
